ownershipCoverage.rule: Main players are those projected above 0 points who are not listed out; a source is used when the players it names hold at least 80% of their total projected points.

recipes.projection: Blended projection = weighted mean of TwoGun x1, TwoGun's own DraftKings projection, used as he publishes it. Weights renormalise over the sources that cover each player; coverage is the covering weight as a share of the total enabled weight. Coverage under 50% keeps the number from the sources that do cover the player and is flagged "thin"; it is never pulled toward a typical score for the salary. A player no ticked source covers has no projection: it is left blank, flagged "no projection" (0 when the injury report lists him out, on IR, doubtful or suspended); his DraftKings average per game never stands in.
recipes.scoring: DraftKings scoring from stat lines; 100/300-yard bonuses paid as 3 x probability from a lognormal (cv rush 0.55, rec 0.55, pass 0.30); DST points-allowed from a normal around the opponent's implied total (SD 9.5, shutout rate unvalidated)

rows.name: Ja'Marr Chase

injury.comment: Chase caught 10 of 12 targets for 155 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.
injury.longComment: The superstar wideout hit the ground running in Madrid, capping Cincinnati's first drive with a 47-yard touchdown catch from Joe Burrow. It was Chase's fourth straight game getting into the end zone, a stretch in which he's delivered a stellar 32-435-4 line on 45 targets, and Sunday's 155 receiving yards were a season high. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North battle against the Steelers.

rows.projHow: TwoGun 22.62 is the only source covering Ja'Marr Chase, his own DraftKings projection, used as he publishes it.

rows.name: Joe Burrow

injury.comment: Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. He added seven yards and a TD on three carries.
injury.longComment: It was a nearly flawless performance from Burrow, as he hit Ja'Marr Chase for a 47-yard score in the first quarter and tossed a pair of shorter TDs to Tee Higgins later in the contest. The superstar QB also got into the end zone on a goal-line sneak in the second quarter. It's the fourth straight game in which Burrow has produced at least four touchdowns, an incredible stretch in which he's completed 77.0 percent of his passes for 1,215 yards with a 16:3 TD:INT plus two more scores on the ground. The Bengals, not coincidentally, are 4-0 in that span. Burrow will look to stay locked in for a big AFC North clash against the Steelers in Week 10.

rows.projHow: TwoGun 23.52 is the only source covering Joe Burrow, his own DraftKings projection, used as he publishes it.

rows.name: Tee Higgins

injury.comment: Higgins caught five of six targets for 32 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over Atlanta.
injury.longComment: While he didn't see big volume, Higgins made his opportunities count, connecting with Joe Burrow on a four-yard TD in the second quarter and an eight-yard score in the third. Higgins has hit paydirt five times in the last three games, and on the season he's produced a 48-758-6 line on 67 targets through eight contests. He'll look to extend his scoring streak in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North clash with the Steelers.

rows.projHow: TwoGun 18.19 is the only source covering Tee Higgins, his own DraftKings projection, used as he publishes it.

rows.name: Jaylen Warren

injury.comment: Warren rushed 17 times for 143 yards and a touchdown and brought in one of two targets for no gain in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.
injury.longComment: Warren tied his single-game career high in rushing yards with Sunday's performance, which was partly fueled by a season-long 51-yard run. Warren now has back-to-back 100-yard efforts on the ground for the first time this season, and he snapped a brief two-game rushing TD drought Sunday with a one-yard run early in the third quarter that closed out the scoring for the afternoon. Warren is already up to 704 rushing yards on a career-best 5.9 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road showdown against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15, following a Week 8 bye.

rows.projHow: TwoGun 17.94 is the only source covering Jaylen Warren, his own DraftKings projection, used as he publishes it.

rows.name: Aaron Rodgers

injury.comment: Rodgers completed 13 of 25 passes for 172 yards with no touchdowns and one interception in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Jaylen Warren spearheaded the Steelers' attack with 143 rushing yards and a touchdown, and backfield mate Rico Dowdle added 56 yards and a score of his own. When combined with a highly effective effort by Pittsburgh's defense, there wasn't much production required of Rodgers and the air attack after much busier games leading into Sunday. Rodgers finished with season-low figures in completions, pass attempts, completion percentage and passing yards while failing to throw a touchdown pass for the first time since Week 2, but he's highly likely to revert to his prior pass-heavy ways in a Week 10 road showdown against the Bengals on Sunday night, Nov. 15, following a Week 8 bye.

rows.projHow: TwoGun 17.06 is the only source covering Aaron Rodgers, his own DraftKings projection, used as he publishes it.

rows.name: Chase Brown

injury.comment: Brown carried the ball nine times for 57 yards and caught all three of his targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.
injury.longComment: Samaje Perine actually saw more volume on the ground with 11 carries for 43 yards, but most of his workload came in the fourth quarter as the Bengals were grinding down the clock. Brown has yet to top 80 rushing yards in a game this season and he hasn't gotten into the end zone since Week 1, a disappointing first half of the year for a running back who amassed at least 1,300 scrimmage yards with double-digit scores each of the prior two campaigns. Brown will look for an opportunity to break out in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North battle against the Steelers.

rows.projHow: TwoGun 17.03 is the only source covering Chase Brown, his own DraftKings projection, used as he publishes it.

rows.name: DK Metcalf

injury.comment: Metcalf brought in one of six targets for four yards in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Aaron Rodgers put up a season low in completions, pass attempts, passing yards and completion percentage Sunday, and Metcalf's production was part of the collateral damage. The veteran wideout did see a team high in targets, but the fact he did next to nothing with them led to season lows in catches and receiving yards. Metcalf has had a handful of splash plays over the first half of the season and has two games of more than 90 receiving yards, but he's averaging a career-low 11.5 yards per catch and has just a single touchdown reception heading into the Week 9 bye.

rows.projHow: TwoGun 13.85 is the only source covering DK Metcalf, his own DraftKings projection, used as he publishes it.

injury.longComment: Bernard led the team in catches, reeling in multiple passes for the fifth straight week and sixth time overall this year. The wide receiver has built a strong rapport with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but it's unclear what Bernard's workload will look like after the Steelers have a chance to regroup and potentially acquire another pass catcher during the team's bye week in Week 9.

injury.comment: McPherson went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts while making all four of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.
injury.longComment: McPherson was able to convert multiple field-goal tries in a game for the first time since Week 3, nailing a 57-yarder in the final moments of the first half before later adding a 43-yard make in the fourth quarter.
